## Why this change is needed

International Markets needs to explain countries' economic and market conditions and projected paths immediately. The previous presentation gave saved research and comparison tools too much prominence and left the central analysis difficult to understand.

## Resulting experience

- World Brief leads with the actual world GDP projection and its publication/cutoff dates.
- Seven country assessments lead with eligible national-bank research, followed by growth and annual-inflation paths, policy decisions, external/fiscal context, observed market conditions, transmission channels, and conditions that would change the thesis.
- Country conditions identify the thesis and evidence they depend on. Corrected forecasts, conflicting national policy evidence, and stale commentary requalify the visible conclusions.
- Comparison, history and saved-research tools remain subordinate. Existing navigation, assistant ownership, keyboard/history behavior and native source disclosures are preserved.
- Responsive desktop/mobile layouts support dark/light and English/Chinese, including 320px chart and policy-detail legibility.

## Research and backend

The increment adds an explicitly registered October 2026 WEO table parser, an immutable forecast-publication archive, typed national-policy evidence, and evidence-linked country interpretation. The ordinary International collection/build path integrates them; no parallel publication service is introduced.

There are 37 archived publications, including October WEO growth/inflation/current-account paths, available fiscal/debt paths, the world GDP aggregate, earlier growth editions, and separate CBC forecasts. Cross-provider forecasts are not mislabeled as IMF revisions. India's fiscal-year labels, Japan's nonconsolidated gross-debt note and the Euro Area's adjusted current-account definition remain explicit.

The UK Bank Rate and Taiwan discount-rate decisions retain named instruments, decision/publication/effective dates, votes where available, and the bank's own rationale. Monthly policy observations have separate time and comparability qualification. Conflicting evidence at different official URLs or with bank display-name aliases withholds the associated country thesis and conditions.

Collector failures retain qualified prior records and source receipts. The CBC values were verified from its full official page, but the connected-host download failed TLS validation; no successful CBC raw download or raw-byte hash is claimed. Fiscal/debt coverage is still missing for KR/TW/IN/AU, and no newer RBI decision was admitted without adequate primary evidence.
